title: Finite coefficient extension and mixed realization coherence
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. Module sheaves, sheaf tensor products, derived categories and cohomology are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,A)$ for the completed integral category including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and $Q:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=\mathcal C_X[1/\varpi]$ for its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. A rational module sheaf is constructible when on a finite locally closed stratification it is pro-etale locally finite free [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Write $F_X(K)=E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$ and $J_X(QK)=F_X(K)$, $J_X(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)$ for the functor specified in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with arbitrary ramification, put $A_L=\mathcal O_L$, $B_{L,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_L/\varpi_L^n)_X$ and $L_X=B_{L,X}[1/\varpi_L]$, and define $J_{L,X}$ by the same formulas. For raw scalar extension $T_{L/E}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], there is a natural isomorphism
$$\theta_{L/E,X}:J_{L,X}T_{L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}(L_X\otimes^L_{E_X}-)J_{E,X}.$$
It is the balanced identification through $L_X\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K$ on an integral representative, using the actual integral functor $B_{L,X}\otimes^L_{B_{E,X}}K$ and the continuous coefficient maps of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations]. On K-flat representatives the comparison flattens $(l\otimes b)\otimes k$ to $lb\otimes k$, with inverse inserting $1$; it respects raw fractions since every nonzero scalar of $E$ becomes invertible in $L$. For $E\subset L\subset M$ its successive-extension diagram commutes with the specified raw scalar associators: both routes flatten $m\otimes l\otimes k$ to $ml\otimes k$; the identity and four-field pentagon diagrams commute as well. For any scheme map $g:X'\to X$ between schemes satisfying the hypotheses, the square comparing $\theta$ and the specific $\alpha_g$ of [lem-per-rational-realization-pullback-comparison] commutes with the scalar/pullback comparison of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The integral coefficient square is the finite-quotient-normalized one; after localization the balanced map on both routes sends $l'\otimes b'\otimes k$ to $l'b'\otimes g^{-1}k$. These equalities hold with the completion units, ambient pullback composition comparisons and all successive coefficient associators, using [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. No pair-category descent or unramified-extension assumption is used.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; expanded finite-extension balancing and mixed coherence, pp. 58,61-62

proof.text: Use rationalBalancedCoefficient and its section and square theorems. Construct the comparison from rationalBalancedTheta. Expand its component as the object transports, S, T inverse, and the inverse source object transport; cancel the adjacent transports and T inverse followed by T to obtain the integral normalization. For any two scalar comparison records, sectionwise evaluation determines their coefficient maps. Their integral normalizations determine their theta components by cancellation of isomorphisms. Every raw object is the rationalization of its integral object, so the two natural isomorphisms, hence the records, agree. Substitute the canonical record into the declared balanced tower, identity and normalized tower equations. This proves rationalRealizationScalarCoherence, rationalRealizationScalarTower, rationalRealizationScalarUnit and rationalRealizationStageTower without changing their statements. For the derived pentagon, apply rationalMixedPentagon to identity geometric pullback, cancel zeta, and transport along the canonical geometric unitor by naturality. The raw pentagon is rationalBalancedPentagon, with the definitionally equal reassociated coefficient inclusion.

source.place: Tags 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.8.2 and Proposition 6.8.14; parent retained steps 1-4

proof.text: Apply the completed-unit-square lemma to the same coefficient inclusion and $g$. It supplies $\kappa$, the reflected comparison $\widehat\beta=\Lambda_L(\beta)\kappa$, and $\widehat\beta C(\gamma_E)=\gamma_L\beta$ for the actual finite-quotient units. The required finite-freeness and positive ramification hypotheses are included, and the comparisons are those of the given scalar functor.

Apply rationalScalarMixedUnitCancellation for the canonical scalar comparisons, after uniqueness identifies every supplied scalar comparison with the canonical record. Its zeta and beta inverses give the ambient and raw mixed comparisons. Identify the ambient strict/intrinsic completion comparison on complete objects with the restricted one by uniqueness, so the inverse strict beta is exactly rationalScalarStrictPullComparison. The existing completion-unit square then gives completion_units. Expand the raw beta component, invert its object transports, and cancel beta and zeta in the mixed compatibility equation. Conversely turn any supplied mixed record into the cancellation record by these inverse operations. Applying rationalMixedCoefficientTower and reversing its isomorphism square gives rationalRealizationScalarMixedTower. For identity pullback, its normalized site comparison is the canonical first projection. Maps out of rational module pullback are determined by the tensor-unit sections through the composite ordinary adjunction. Hence the recorded ordinary identity comparison equals the canonical one; the derived computation normalization then identifies the ambient unitor on every cochain representative. Reverse rationalMixedGeometricIdentity after this identification.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15, pp. 61-62; explicit completion-unit cancellation and mixed pasting, parent retained steps 8-9 (agent expansion)

proof.text: For rationalScalarPullIdentity apply rationalPullbackIdentityCoherence. Retain its normalized ordinary, ambient and raw unitors and take the canonical first-projection identity fiber product as site comparison. Specialize the ordinary tensor-generator formula at coefficient one, and remove the identity cochain comparison from its derived formula. Evaluate its natural alpha compatibility equation at each raw object. For rationalScalarPullComposition, invert the ordinary, ambient and raw comparisons supplied by rationalPullbackCompositionCoherence. The ordinary inverse formula follows from the coefficient-one tensor-generator formula and naturality across the site compositor; restriction along the site isomorphism cancels. Invert the derived counit equation and raw normalized-component equation. Cancel the three strict units in the completed-unit equation to identify the inverse completed comparison with rationalScalarStrictPullComp, then invert the alpha compatibility equation.

For rationalRealizationScalarMixedComp, identify the supplied scalar records with the canonical records by rationalScalarComparison_unique. Identify any supplied ordinary geometric compositor with the inverse of the canonical one: the coefficient-one formula of rationalPullbackCompositionCoherence, naturality across the canonical site compositor and cancellation of restriction along its inverse give precisely its ordinary_units formula. The composite ordinary adjunction makes the tensor-unit generators jointly determining. To identify the ambient compositors, resolve an arbitrary cochain representative by a flat-term K-flat complex. The algebraic inverse-image presentation and preservation of flat-term K-flat complexes make the direct rational pullback computation counit invertible on this representative. Compose the supplied normalization with the canonical one; the inverse ordinary maps cancel under Q. Cancel the computation counit. Naturality along the resolution isomorphism transports the equality to every representative, and localization extensionality identifies the natural isomorphisms. Apply rationalMixedGeometricComposition to the three supplied mixed records converted to cancellation records. Their zeta maps are the inverses of their ambient maps. Take the inverse of the resulting isomorphism equality and replace the canonical compositors by the identified supplied ones. This is exactly the asserted mixed-composition equality.
